claims.text: Thermal annealing in an appropriate temperature-time window will promote nanoscale Cr/V-rich precipitates in a magnetic high-entropy alloy.
Nanoscale Cr/V-rich precipitates will increase coercive field by enhancing magnetic domain-wall pinning.
The as-deposited alloy has a nanocrystalline or ultrafine grain structure.
The as-deposited alloy initially has minimal precipitate formation.
A treatment window around 1023–1073 K is suitable for the proposed annealing intervention.
The proposed 1023–1073 K window is below the threshold for significant grain growth.
An optimized annealing duration will induce nanoscale precipitate formation.
Annealing must be performed in an inert atmosphere to prevent oxidation.
The coercivity-enhancing effect requires preservation of the fine-grained microstructure.
Cr and V can segregate to grain boundaries under the proposed conditions.
The annealing treatment will produce Cr/V-rich precipitates at grain boundaries and triple junctions.
The precipitates will inhibit domain-wall motion relative to the less-segregated as-deposited baseline.
Annealed samples will have measurably greater coercive field than matched untreated samples.
The coercivity increase can occur without detrimental grain growth or loss of magnetic-phase integrity.
The untreated as-deposited baseline has lower coercivity than the proposed annealed state.
Excessive annealing temperature or duration may cause significant grain growth or unwanted phase transformations.
Grain growth or unwanted phase transformations may negate the proposed pinning benefit and reduce coercivity.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant coercivity increase, operationally exemplified as greater than 10%, is designated as a falsifying result.
